summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Ironwood Systems' partnerships, cloud and security leads. Discussed reseller model, integration options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), pilot scope, security/compliance requirements, and a technical deep-dive next steps. Customer is evaluating partners to support a managed SaaS offering that bundles Redwood inference inside their platform; timeline is target pilot in Q1 2027. Main concerns: data residency, KMS integration, latency SLAs for inference, and reseller economics.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:08
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SA), Raj Patel (Ironwood Head of Partnerships), Lena Hofstad (Cloud Solutions Lead), Marco Silva (CTO), Tara Nguyen (Security Lead), Owen Brooks (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Quick alignment on reseller commercial model and pilot framing; security artifacts requested; technical deep dive scheduled.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE here. we've got Daniel and Priya with me from the tech side. careful about time, so we'll run through goals, ironwood's needs, then dig into technical constraints then next steps.
01:12 - Raj Patel: Thanks Maya, yeah, appreciate it. quick intro from our side — i'm Raj, i run partnerships. lena is our cloud lead, marco heads platform, tara is security and owen handles product. we're evaluating partners to embed inference into our SaaS offering.
02:05 - Daniel Ortiz: Nice to meet you all. quick context: Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and a private VPC/private deployment option. Typical partner paths are reseller + pilot, or direct dedicated deployments depending on compliance needs.
03:20 - Lena Hofstad: our basic ask is we want a partner who can be a white-label-ish backend for inference, so we can surface features directly in our product. key constraints: latency under 120ms for small prompts, token cost we need to model into our pricing, and data residency for EU customers.
04:10 - Marco Silva: also, multi-tenancy isolation is important — we want to ensure our tenant data doesn't leak, and for some enterprise customers we might need an on-prem or private VPC option.
05:00 - Priya Nair: totally. couple of quick clarifying q's: is your plan to resell as a managed service where Ironwood bills end-customers, or will Redwood invoice directly?
05:20 - Raj Patel: ideally Ironwood would bill — we want to own the customer relationship, but may negotiate pricing with Redwood. that's why the reseller economics doc will be important.
06:00 - Maya Chen: we can certainly support reseller/commercial arrangements — we'll follow up with a one-pager and a draft price band. question for Daniel: on the infra side, for Ironwood's latency targets do you think hosted API with caching could meet 120ms?
06:25 - Daniel Ortiz: depends on model and region. if you're using small Llama-family style models or optimized quantized variants, hosted can hit low latencies with prefix caching and our continuous batching tuned. for consistent sub-120ms, many customers choose Dedicated reserved pools in-region. Also private VPC gives you more control but has deployment lead time.
07:30 - Lena Hofstad: Deployment lead time — how long to get a private VPC up and running with our networking and KMS?
07:45 - Priya Nair: typically 4-6 weeks once contracts and infra details are cleared for a private deployment; dedicated reserved pool is faster, usually in the 2-week range for provisioning if capacity is available.
08:20 - Tara Nguyen: what about KMS integration? we have a vendor-managed KMS and need to ensure keys never leave our control.
08:40 - Priya Nair: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments. for hosted, we can do bring-your-own-key to some extent but there are caveats — will share security FAQ.
09:10 - Marco Silva: audit logs — our enterprise customers require exportable request logs for a rolling 12 months. can you provide that?
09:30 - Daniel Ortiz: yes, Redwood Console can export per-route traces, token costs, and request logs. for private deployments we'll surface more detailed logs; for hosted we have retention tiers (add-on for longer retention).
10:05 - Owen Brooks: curious about model variants — do you host open models or closed ones? we need to know about licensing and model updates impacting behavior.
10:25 - Maya Chen: we host curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles, and we can pin specific model versions for deterministic behavior. model updates are a controlled rollout with canary and A/B tests to avoid regressions.
11:35 - Raj Patel: timeline — we're targetting a pilot in Q1 2027, ideally Jan-Feb. what would you recommend as a pilot scope?
12:05 - Daniel Ortiz: recommended pilot: 2-week pilot with a small reserved Dedicated pool, sample 10k monthly active users' inference traffic replicated, run latency and cost benchmarks, and compare hosted vs dedicated. That gives you data to model pricing.
12:50 - Lena Hofstad: cost — can you share typical per-token bands for small/medium models?
13:10 - Maya Chen: we'll send example pricing ranges; rough — hosted rates vary, dedicated unit economics depend on commit level. we'll include a sample cost model spreadsheet.
14:00 - Tara Nguyen: security questionnaire — we'll need SOC2 docs and answers to a standard security RFI.
14:20 - Priya Nair: we'll attach SOC2 excerpts and a filled security checklist; for private deployments we can provide more detailed audit logs and attestation.
15:05 - Marco Silva: on performance, what measures do you provide to ensure KV cache and prefix caching work well with multi-tenant workloads? we don't want noisy neighbors hurting latency.
15:30 - Daniel Ortiz: we have workload-aware batching, tenant-aware KV cache sharding and options to pin hot tenants to dedicated GPUs in Dedicated mode. For hosted, we do smart routing and soft isolation but dedicated gives stronger isolation guarantees.
16:45 - Raj Patel: any red flags for us to watch when integrating? network egress, VPC peering complexity?
17:05 - Priya Nair: VPC peering and routing can be the most friction. also certificate rotation and KMS endpoints. we'll provide a network diagram template.
18:12 - Owen Brooks: is there a middleware — like an SDK — you'd recommend for our product team to integrate quickly?
18:25 - Daniel Ortiz: yes, we have SDKs and REST endpoints. plus a small reference implementation for token-level billing and routing hooks we can share.
19:10 - Lena Hofstad: data residency: can we ensure EU data stays in EU regions for our EU tenants?
19:30 - Priya Nair: yes — routing by region is part of the platform; with private deployment you can fully restrict region. hosted: we support region pinning for enterprise tiers.
20:05 - Raj Patel: competitor question — we've seen VertexCloud and Cloudium pitch something similar. how do you differentiate on reliability and cost?
20:30 - Maya Chen: our differentiators are production-first runtime optimizations, transparent performance profiles, and cost-aware controls like automatic batching and caching suggestions. plus dedicated+private options with the same API. we'll share benchmark docs.
21:40 - Marco Silva: will you support on-prem air-gapped installs if a customer needs it?
21:55 - Priya Nair: we do an on-prem pack for regulated customers, but that typically requires a longer engagement and additional support.
22:40 - Lena Hofstad: for the pilot, we want to run three tests: latency under 50 tokens, end-to-end 95th percentile; throughput sustained for typical bursts; and cost per 1k prompts. can Redwood provide tooling to run these tests?
23:05 - Daniel Ortiz: yes, we can provide an eval harness and synthetic workload generator, plus sample prompts and metrics dashboards.
24:12 - Raj Patel: any legal/compliance items we should start now? data processing addendum, standard contractual clauses for EU?
24:30 - Maya Chen: we'll have our legal team send DPA and SCCs; for private deployments there's additional paperwork.
25:10 - Tara Nguyen: one more on encryption-in-transit: do you support mTLS for edge connections?
25:25 - Priya Nair: mTLS is supported for private and dedicated endpoints; hosted supports TLS and optional mTLS for enterprise tiers.
26:15 - Owen Brooks: question on billing: can we get consolidated invoices per month for all customers with breakout by tenant?
26:40 - Maya Chen: yes, consolidated billing with per-tenant usage CSVs is possible for partners/resellers.
27:05 - Raj Patel: great. can we talk about SLA and uptimes?
27:25 - Daniel Ortiz: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort tiers with paid SLA add-ons. we'll share SLA docs.
28:40 - Marco Silva: from a tech integration standpoint, we want to run the pilot in our staging environment with masked data. any pointers?
29:00 - Priya Nair: we recommend synthetic data plus a small anonymized sample; we'll provide guidance on masking and prefix caching warmup strategies.
30:12 - (brief cross-talk, people joining)
31:00 - Maya Chen: ok wrapping a bit on timeline: next steps i heard: we'll send reseller one-pager, pricing bands, SOC2 excerpts, and an invite for the infra deep dive. customer will share pilot workload details. anything else?
31:30 - Raj Patel: sounds right. please include the network diagram and SDK examples.
31:45 - Daniel Ortiz: i'll own the technical deep dive and bring a template for the benchmark harness.
32:00 - Lena Hofstad: we'll aim to have our pilot spec to you by Dec 2.
32:20 - Maya Chen: perfect. any blockers?
32:30 - Tara Nguyen: nothing critical, just want to review SOC2 and ensure KMS path.
32:45 - Priya Nair: we'll prioritize that and note the KMS caveats for hosted vs private.
33:10 - Raj Patel: ok last question — for multi-tenant billing, if we resell do you offer per-customer nested invoicing or do we need to build our own pass-through?
33:30 - Maya Chen: we support both: reseller consolidated invoicing or per-customer billing via sub-account CSVs and billing APIs.
34:01 - Owen Brooks: minor nit: how do you handle model rollbacks if a canary causes a regression?
34:15 - Daniel Ortiz: we have canary rollouts and an automatic rollback policy tied to evals; Redwood Optimize also alerts on quality regressions tied to prompt sets.
35:00 - (longer discussion on model management, some interruptions)
45:40 - (people return after side conversations)
45:55 - Maya Chen: ok i'll recap in the email with links: partnership one-pager, pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 redacted, SDK repo link (private), network diagram template, and calendar invite for deep dive.
46:20 - Raj Patel: thanks, appreciate it. we'll review docs and get pilot spec by Dec 2.
46:50 - Lena Hofstad: one follow-up: can you share an example of dedicated pool sizing for 50 req/s with 90ms p95?
47:05 - Daniel Ortiz: yes - i'll include a sizing table and sample GPU types; depends on model choice and quantization.
47:45 - Marco Silva: any final security clarifications?
48:00 - Tara Nguyen: just want to confirm retention of logs and the ability to get redacted request logs for compliance — you said that's an add-on?
48:20 - Priya Nair: correct, long-term retention is an add-on for hosted; private deployments typically include more control over retention.
49:10 - Raj Patel: ok thanks everyone.
49:25 - Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the deck and next steps.
49:40 - (meeting ends)

Post-meeting notes: Links referenced (to be attached in follow-up email): partnership-one-pager.pdf, reseller-pricing-template.xlsx, soc2-excerpts.pdf, redwood-sdk-private-repo (link), network-diagram-template.pdf, eval-harness.zip

Final recap (auto): Pilot 2 weeks on dedicated pool -> benchmarks for latency/cost. Redwood to provide security and commercial docs. Tech deep dive scheduled next week to size Dedicated pool.
